props.name: aria-label
props.description: The calendar's name, which starts each grid's name, such as "Delivery date, October 2026". Name a calendar that stands alone with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The ids of the elements that name the calendar, in place of `aria-label`. Each grid is then named by those elements and its month heading.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts: a `Calendar.Header` with `Calendar.DecrementMonth`, `Calendar.VisibleRangeHeading` and `Calendar.IncrementMonth`, then `Calendar.Months`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The day selected first, when the calendar owns its value. Takes what `value` takes. With neither `value` nor `defaultValue`, the calendar opens on today's month. Only the first client effect reads the clock, so the server and the hydrating render write each month's frame, the weekday row over six weeks of empty days, hidden from assistive technology, and the calendar hydrates without a mismatch. It keeps that height for a six-week month and shrinks by a row or two for a shorter one. Today is marked from the same effect on, never in a server render, and the mark moves at midnight.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether nothing in the calendar responds: no day takes focus and the month buttons are disabled.

props.name: firstDayOfWeek
props.description: The weekday each row starts on. Defaults to the locale's: Sunday in en-US, Monday in the Nordic locales.

props.name: isDateUnavailable
props.description: Days the user may focus but not select, such as fully booked ones. Return `true` to refuse a day. Keep the function's identity stable across renders, since every day re-renders when it changes.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: The last selectable day, taking what `minValue` takes. Days after it are disabled and never take focus, the keyboard stops at it, and its name ends ", Last available date".

props.name: minValue
props.description: The first selectable day: a Temporal PlainDate, PlainDateTime or ZonedDateTime from any implementation. A date-time bound counts from its own wall-clock day. Days before it are disabled and never take focus, the keyboard stops at it, and its name ends ", First available date". A month button whose page has no selectable day is disabled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the user selects a day, by pressing it or with Enter or Space, with the day as this runtime's `Temporal.PlainDate`. `details.reason` is `"day-press"` or `"keyboard"`, and `details.event` and `details.trigger` are the DOM event and the day's button. Canceling with `details.cancel()` keeps the value unchanged; focus stays on the day. `details.getValidationError()` returns `null` here, since the calendar lets the user select only days that pass.

props.name: onVisibleRangeChange
props.description: Called when the visible months change by a month button or the keyboard, with the new first month. `details.reason` is `"increment-press"`, `"decrement-press"` or `"keyboard"`. Canceling with `details.cancel()` keeps the months shown: a month button press does nothing, and a key that would page leaves focus on the day it was on.

props.name: pageBehavior
props.description: How the month buttons page a multi-month view, and how far the view moves when the keyboard leaves it: `"visible"` by every visible month, `"single"` by one.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user may move around the months but not change the value.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected day, when the parent owns it: a `Temporal.PlainDate` from any implementation. A server component cannot pass one, since it reaches the client as ISO text, which the calendar refuses with a `TypeError`: build the value in a client component. `null` selects nothing. Import `@elmeragroup/fuse/temporal-polyfill` on the server and in the browser for engines without `Temporal`, and type-check with TypeScript 6 and an `esnext` lib, as `/quick-start#temporal` shows.

props.name: visibleMonths
props.description: How many months show side by side, wrapping onto new rows when the host is narrow. Pick it from the viewport in the host, such as one month on a phone and two on a desktop; the server renders the count the host passes there. A whole number from 1: a fraction truncates, and anything below 1 or not a finite number shows one month, with a warning in development. Arrow keys move focus from one month's grid into the next without paging.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes, merged last through `cn`. A `px-*` class replaces the label padding only. The icon side keeps its own padding, which `has-data-[icon=inline-start]:pl-*` or `has-data-[icon=inline-end]:pr-*` replaces.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: isPending
props.description: Marks an action in flight. The button blocks activation, dims, and stamps `data-pending` and `aria-busy`. It stays in the focus order, so a keyboard user is still on it when the result arrives. `focusableWhenDisabled={false}` takes it out of the focus order. `aria-busy` announces nothing, so say what is happening in the label, such as "Saving", or in a `role="status"` region outside the button. Put a label that changes with the state in its own element, such as `{label}`: page translation replaces a bare text child with its own nodes, so React's update to the old text node never shows.

props.name: isVisuallyDisabled
props.description: Makes the button look and announce disabled while it stays interactive. It stamps `aria-disabled`, and an explicit `aria-disabled` wins. Click, keyboard and focus still work, and a Tooltip on the button still opens. Use it for an action that explains on activation why it is unavailable.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: onClick
props.description: Runs before the page changes. Call `event.preventBaseUIHandler()` in it to stop the change. The button is disabled, and stays focusable, when no page lies that way within the bounds.

props.name: onIntent
props.description: Fires once when the pointer's predicted path enters the inflated hit rect, for prefetching. Browsers without pointer prediction never fire it.

props.name: pendingIndicator
props.description: What a pending button shows in its leading icon position. When you omit it, a spinner shows there and the button's leading and bare icons hide, while a `data-icon="inline-end"` icon stays. A node replaces the spinner and does not animate on its own. `null` or `false` shows nothing and hides nothing, so the call site draws its own pending state. Fade that content with `group-data-pending/button:opacity-0`, not `invisible`, which drops the label from the accessible name, and give an overlay no `data-icon`.

props.name: predictionZoneSize
props.description: Pixels added to every side of the hit rect when predicting pointer intent.
